text:
otto: quick sync from today's late-night canary. saw intermittent latency spikes when we drained hosts that hold sticky sessions. pattern not just KV-miss; routing oscillation + head-of-line effects.
otto: p95 moved ~1.8x for ~5% of requests in the cohort for ~9m.
sasha: timeline? was this during a scale-down or a deploy?
otto: both. autoscaler trimmed and we rotated a variant in the same window. sessions pinned by affinity kept hitting partly-evicted nodes; targets got a burst of cold reads and then queueing.
lin: i sketched a different angle: instead of immediate split/probe/prefetch variants we've used elsewhere, try a "decaying-trust + warm-lane" pattern. core idea: each host/variant has a trust score for a cohort that decays on drain/eviction. routing uses warm-lane for low-trust targets to accept lightweight warm RPCs rather than full request routing.
sasha: warm-lane sounds like prefetch-led but emphasizes trust. how does decaying-trust evolve?
lin: simple rules: on normal serve trust += alpha (cap 1.0). on drain signal trust *= decay_factor (e.g., 0.5). while trust < threshold we route only a tiny fraction of traffic to target OR send warm-lane ops that prefetch prefixes. trust increments on successful warm-lane hits and drops on probe failures or high p95.
cal: sounds promising. what signals to compute fallback? we need compact decision surface for the routing plane.
lin: minimal signals: trust_score, warm_hit_rate, target_p95_ratio. Fallback if target_p95_ratio > p95_thresh OR trust fails to recover after N windows. Implemented locally per-cohort. central controller only issues policy changes or global stop.
otto: config example (proto will store strings):
```json
{"strategy":"decay-trust-warm-lane","initial_trust":"1.0","drain_decay":"0.5","warm_lane_fraction":"0.02","max_warm_lane":"0.15","trust_recovery_step":"0.05","p95_ratio_threshold":"1.5","stale_windows_before_fallback":"3"}
```
sasha: warm-lane fraction of 2% seems safe to start. warm-lane ops should be non-blocking and not count against SLAs. we need instrumentation to track warm-call latency and whether it actually populated local KV.
lin: implementation notes: 1) small per-cohort state machine in the router storing trust score and last N probe outcomes; 2) warm-lane RPC to target that accepts a prefix list and returns a hit/miss hint (best-effort); 3) if warm-call succeeded for X consecutive calls increase trust and bump routing weight; 4) on failure we exponentially backoff trust recovery and decrease routing weight.
cal: fallback severity levels? full rollback is blunt. propose levels: 0=ok, 1=soft-hold (reduce commit rate), 2=soft-rollback (route back to old variant for new sessions), 3=hard-rollback (global rollback).
otto: controllers can escalate levels automatically if fallback conditions persist or an operator can force levels. deploy-bot: will emit level-change events when controller adjusts severity.
sasha: observability: Console needs a compact "trust view" per cohort showing trust_score, warm_hit_rate, target_p95_ratio, current severity, last_reason. also a time-series of warm-lane RPC success and sampled traces.
lin: retention should be short for warm-call traces to control cost. add a sampled flame for warm->serve path correlated with host drain events.
cal: testing plan: unit tests for state transitions, small sim that models prefix reuse vs prefetch cost and trust dynamics, canary with synthetic long-chat sessions, and a chaos test that injects delayed KV responses on targets.
sasha: runbook: on severity >=2 trigger, ops should check the trust view, recent drain events, warm-hit ratios, and queue depth. actions: 1) pause rollout controller, 2) expand warm-lane to max for a short time to attempt recovery, 3) if no improvement escalate to soft-rollback.
otto: small UX ask: let SREs manually nudge trust_score per cohort in Console for VIP tenants. also tenant-priority lanes so high-reuse tenants get higher warm-lane pct.
lin: perf cost: warm-lane RPCs add extra ops but are cheap compared to full requests. simulator will quantify additional network + prefetch overhead vs avoided rollback cost.
cal: i'll own wiring of severity events to the deploy stream and a small alert: trust_score < 0.3 and target_p95_ratio > 1.4 for >5m -> page oncall.
sasha: i'll add Console panels and an explainer. lin: i'll write the RFC with the state machine diagram, proto config, and simulator results. otto: i'll draft the runbook and coordinate a staged canary next week. deploy-bot: scheduled-canary: job 2024-04-25T03:00Z created for variant v11; will post trust-level and fallback events to eng-runtime.
cal: thanks all. feels like a lower-risk path vs immediate rollback. :thumbsup:
